what_it_does: High-frequency radar and wireless systems (125–170 GHz, or sub-terahertz) need phase shifters—circuits that change the timing of radio waves so antenna arrays can beam signals in different directions. This chip uses an 'outphasing' technique: instead of modulating phase and power separately (which wastes energy), it splits the modulation into two constant-power signals that combine to create the desired phase and amplitude, similar to how two angled pushes can create motion in any direction. Built in SiGe BiCMOS technology (a silicon-germanium process), it automatically corrects for manufacturing variations and temperature drift.
